approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in TN
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Panel schedule showing existing and proposed circuits
Wire gauge and breaker size for each new circuit
Electrical diagram or one-line drawing (required for panel upgrades)
Utility disconnect location marked on plans

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed commercial contractor pulls the permit on behalf of the owner, and the contractor's Metro Nashville registration/license information must appear on the application. For electrical work, Nashville uses its own Metro electrical license/registration process; Tennessee does not use a state electrical license for this city permit path.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Metro Nashville Codes Administration
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Nashville Metro Codes requires contractor registration before pulling permits. Registration is annual, and an expired registration can block permit submission without a clear error. Verify current registration status at nashville.gov/departments/codes before applying.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit application without verifying current Metro Nashville contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently.
Trying to pull only trade permits and skipping the building permit for the occupancy change and tenant improvement.
Under-scoping the electrical work — panel changes and any new circuits must be shown on the electrical permit and plans.
any ventilation or heat-producing equipment requirements.
Starting demolition before the building permit and trade permits are issued and posted.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the Metro Nashville Accela portal at If portal scheduling is unavailable for a specific inspection type, call (615) 862-6590. Nashville Metro requires contractor registration to be current before scheduling/submitting; verify registration before booking. Advance notice requirement was not stated in the source context, so confirm with the inspector assigned to your permit.

inspections.description: Reviewer checks occupancy classification, occupant load, egress paths, accessibility, fire separation, finish materials, and whether the proposed bar layout matches the code path for the new use.

Inspector verifies fixture locations, drain/waste/vent sizing, vent routing, water supply routing, trap arm lengths, cleanouts, and that any required backflow or shutoff provisions are in place before walls are closed.

pro_tips: Check your Nashville Metro contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most common avoidable rejection reasons.
Because Nashville has permit backlogs during growth periods, ask whether expedited review is available; the city notes expedited review is typically 50% of the permit fee.
Bring a clean, coordinated plan set that shows the occupancy change, fixture count, and panel schedule together — that cuts down on correction cycles.
If the electrical panel work affects load, include a load calculation up front so the reviewer does not kick it back for missing capacity data.

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: For a commercial bar tenant improvement and occupancy change, zoning and use approval can be a major issue. Verify the space is zoned for bar/alcohol service, confirm any parking or occupancy limits, and check whether a zoning letter or use approval is needed before permit issuance. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for a commercial tenant space, but historic district or overlay rules may still apply.
